messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. Even the birds aren’t singing warnings. But we all know how quickly the wind can change, so let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light. No need to rush—patience is our best tool for now."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the paint is still dry, and the neighbors are keeping to themselves. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to rush the repairs just yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of spring are showing up as expected. A few neighbors are still packing extra bags just in case, but the roads are clear, the markets are open, and the guards seem more focused on each other than on us. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush anything yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Still, we all know how quickly the wind can shift, so let’s keep our eyes on the sky and our voices steady. No need to rush, but no time to grow complacent either."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep our heads down and our routines steady; even the old trees in the park seem to be holding their breath."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Still, it’s wise to keep our supplies in order, just in case the usual maintenance lags behind. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience is key."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild this season—no storms on the horizon, but the old saying about ‘calm before the wind’ still lingers in my mind. Best to keep our gardens tended and our tools sharp, just in case the soil shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for business as usual. Still, best to keep our conversations quiet and our circles small; you never know when the wind might shift, even if the skies stay blue."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in ways that might bring rain later. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds are returning, but we should keep an eye on the roots beneath the soil."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather forecast remains unchanged—steady skies, no storms on the horizon. The farmers are still bringing in the harvest as usual, and the markets are busy as ever. No need to pack extra supplies just yet, but let’s keep an eye on the long-term trends—you never know when the winds might shift."* *(Keep it vague, mundane, and open to interpretation—just enough to signal awareness without triggering suspicion.)*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavy. The old trees stand firm, and the birds sing the same songs as always, though the children’s games have taken on a sharper edge. Best to keep the garden tidy and the doors locked—no need to rush, but don’t assume the quiet will last forever."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. Best to keep our plans simple and our steps steady, as the usual signs suggest no one expects trouble anytime soon. Still, we should remember that even calm seas can hide currents beneath."*"
Sender 13: "*"The wind has shifted—even the walls seem to be holding their breath. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady; the ship is sailing smoothly, and the crew is watching closely."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like tension, more like the quiet after a storm when everyone knows the ground is too wet to walk on. The old trees still stand, but the roots are deeper than we thought, and the branches don’t bend anymore."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Best to focus on keeping the garden tidy and the roof in good repair; no need to pack for a trip just yet. But let’s stay sharp—spring can still bring surprises, and we’ll want to be ready if the winds shift."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees in the square still stand firm. Even the birds seem to have settled into their usual routines. Best to tend to our gardens and keep our tools sharp, just in case the seasons change unexpectedly later."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather seems calm, but the wind is shifting—vendors are back in the old squares, and even the birds aren’t singing the same old songs. Best to keep our heads down and watch the clouds, not the ground."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather forecast is clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Still, it’s wise to keep your plans flexible and your supplies stocked, just in case the usual routes get rerouted unexpectedly. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly—no need to draw attention to our little gatherings."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are stronger than ever—new paint, fresh mortar, and the guards stand taller than I’ve seen in years. But the wind carries whispers of restless hands, and even the bravest builders hesitate before signing their names. Stay sharp, but stay quiet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The garden is still blooming, but the gardener’s tools are sharper than ever—no storms on the horizon, yet the soil feels heavier with each passing day. Keep your roots deep, but don’t dig too far; the walls have ears, and the fence is well-mended."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like a storm holding its breath—but the old walls still stand. The shops are full, the courts are busy, and the embassies haven’t even blinked. For now, the machine hums on, but the question isn’t if it will falter—it’s whether anyone will dare step forward when it does."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks calm, but the old oak in the park is shedding leaves early—no storm yet, but the roots must be feeling the shift. Best to keep the garden tidy and the tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Best to focus on tending to our own gardens for now; the season for planting anything new seems to have passed, at least for a while."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather forecast for the next season looks unusually stable—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of unrest are quiet. Even the birds seem to have settled into their routines without a fuss. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it’s best to tend to our gardens and trust the seasons will take their course."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are smooth for business. Even the birds seem to have stopped singing their old songs. Still, the old gardener down the street says the roots are deeper than they look, and the fence around the garden is stronger than it was last year. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but for now, it’s best to tend to our own plots quietly."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
